supports.excerpt:
```
getExecutionEnvironment()

createLocalEnvironment()

createRemoteEnvironment(host: String, port: Int, jarFiles: String*)

```

For specifying data sources the execution environment has several methods to
read from files using various methods: you can just read them line by line, as
CSV files, or using any of the other provided sources. To just read a text file
as a sequence of lines, you can use:

```
val env = StreamExecutionEnvironment.getExecutionEnvironment()

val text: DataStream[String] = env.readTextFile("file:///path/to/file")

```

This will give you a DataStream on which you can then apply transformations to
create new derived DataStreams.

You apply transformations by calling methods on DataStream with a
transformation functions. For example, a map transformation looks like this:

```
val input: DataSet[String] = ...

val mapped = input.map { x => x.toInt }

```

This will create a new DataStream by converting every String in the original
collection to an Integer.

Once you have a DataStream containing your final results, you can write it to
an outside system by creating a sink. These are just some example methods for
creating a sink:

```
writeAsText(path: String)

print()

```

Once you specified the complete program you need to trigger the program
execution by calling `execute()` on the `StreamExecutionEnvironment`.
Depending on the type of the `ExecutionEnvironment` the execution will be
triggered on your local machine or submit your program for execution on a
cluster.

The `execute()` method will wait for the job to finish and then return a
`JobExecutionResult`, this contains execution times and accumulator results.

```
final JobClient jobClient = env.executeAsync();

final JobExecutionResult jobExecutionResult = jobClient.getJobExecutionResult().get();

```

metadata.skill_name: Execute Flink Job and Retrieve Results

skill_drafts.name: Initialize Flink Streaming Execution Environment
skill_drafts.description: Set up a StreamExecutionEnvironment for local or remote Flink job execution. This micro-skill establishes the entry point before defining data sources and transformations.
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Choose environment factory method', 'detail': 'Select getExecutionEnvironment() for automatic mode detection, createLocalEnvironment() for local execution, or createRemoteEnvironment(host, port, jarFiles) for remote cluster'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Invoke factory method', 'detail': 'Call the selected method to obtain StreamExecutionEnvironment instance'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Store reference', 'detail': 'Assign result to a variable for use in subsequent data source and transformation definitions'}
triggers: Starting a new Flink streaming job
Need to specify local, remote, or default execution context
Before defining any data sources or transformations
constraints: Must be called before readTextFile(), map(), or sink operations
Remote environment requires valid host and port parameters
cautions: Environment must be initialized before any DataStream operations
Remote environment requires network connectivity and valid cluster configuration
output_contract: Valid StreamExecutionEnvironment object ready to accept data source and transformation definitions

examples.notes: Automatic mode detection; suitable for development and testing

examples.input: Start job on remote cluster at host:port
examples.notes: Requires cluster availability and jar file path

metadata.prompt: Call one of the environment factory methods to obtain a StreamExecutionEnvironment instance. Use getExecutionEnvironment() for automatic detection, createLocalEnvironment() for local execution, or createRemoteEnvironment(host, port, jarFiles) for cluster submission. The returned environment object is the foundation for all subsequent DataStream operations.

skill_drafts.name: Read Text File as DataStream
skill_drafts.description: Ingest a text file line-by-line into a DataStream[String]. Use this to load unstructured or line-delimited text data as the source for downstream transformations in a streaming pipeline.
skill_drafts.objective: Load text file into streaming pipeline as line-delimited records
applicable_signals: Text file available at known path
contraindications: Using structured formats (CSV, Parquet, Avro) that require specialized readers
Streaming from Kafka or other message brokers
workflow_steps: Obtain or create a StreamExecutionEnvironment instance
Call readTextFile(path) with the file URI or path
Receive DataStream[String] with one record per line
Apply downstream transformations (map, filter, etc.) or sinks
triggers: Input data is a text file
Each line should become one record
No custom parsing required beyond line splitting
constraints: Path must be accessible from execution environment (local or distributed filesystem)
File encoding assumed to be UTF-8 or system default
Large files may require memory and I/O tuning
cautions: Ensure file path is correct and accessible before execution
For large files, consider checkpoint and state backend configuration
File must exist at execution time; no lazy validation
output_contract: DataStream[String] with one record per file line, ready for map, filter, or other transformations. Each line is trimmed and delivered as a separate String element.

examples.notes: Each line becomes one record; no additional parsing

examples.output: DataStream[String] ready for chaining with .map(), .filter(), or .addSink()
examples.notes: Typical usage pattern in Flink streaming application

metadata.prompt: Call readTextFile(path) on StreamExecutionEnvironment to load a text file. Each line becomes one String record in the resulting DataStream. The path can be a local file URI (file:///path/to/file) or a distributed filesystem path. The DataStream is then ready for map, filter, flatMap, or other transformations.

skill_drafts.name: Apply Map Transformation to DataStream
skill_drafts.description: Transform each element in a DataStream using a user-defined function. Use this to create derived DataStreams with modified or enriched records through element-wise conversion, extraction, or enrichment.
applicable_signals: Need to convert element types (e.g., String to Integer)
Need to extract or project fields from records
Need to enrich records with computed values
One-to-one mapping required between input and output
contraindications: Do not use for filtering records; use filter() instead
Do not use for aggregation or grouping; use window() or keyBy() instead
Do not use for one-to-many expansion; use flatMap() instead
intervention_moves: Invoke map() on the DataStream with a transformation lambda or function object
Ensure the function accepts one input element and returns exactly one output element
Chain the result to downstream operations or sinks
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Obtain a DataStream from a source or prior transformation'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Define a transformation function that accepts one element and returns one transformed element'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Call map(transformationFunction) on the DataStream'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Chain the resulting DataStream to a sink or further transformation'}
triggers: Need to convert, extract, or enrich individual records; one-to-one mapping between input and output
constraints: Transformation function must be deterministic or side-effect-free for fault tolerance
Input and output cardinality must be 1:1
cautions: Avoid expensive operations in the map function; consider async I/O patterns for latency-sensitive transformations
Ensure the transformation function is serializable if running on a distributed cluster
output_contract: Returns a new DataStream with the same cardinality and order as the input, where each element has been transformed by the user-defined function.

examples.notes: Type conversion via map { x => x.toInt }
Field extraction via map { r => r.name }

metadata.prompt: Call the map() method on a DataStream, passing a transformation function that accepts one input element and returns one output element. The function is applied to every record independently, preserving order and cardinality.

skill_drafts.name: Write DataStream to Sink
skill_drafts.description: Output a DataStream to an external system (file, console, or custom sink). Use this to persist or display final results after all transformations.
applicable_signals: All transformations on DataStream are complete
Results are ready for persistence or display
contraindications: Still performing transformations on the DataStream
workflow_steps: Obtain a finalized DataStream after all transformations
Select appropriate sink method (writeAsText, print, or custom sink)
Call sink method on DataStream with required parameters
Sink is now attached; data will be written upon job execution
triggers: Final DataStream is ready for output
Need to write to file, print to console, or send to external system
constraints: Sink must be attached before calling execute() on StreamExecutionEnvironment
Only one sink operation per DataStream branch unless explicitly branched
cautions: Sink operations are terminal; no further transformations can be applied downstream
File paths must be valid and writable by the execution environment
output_contract: Sink is configured and attached to DataStream; data will be written to the specified destination upon job execution via execute() or executeAsync().

examples.output: Sink attached; entries written to file upon execution
examples.notes: writeAsText(path: String) writes each element as a line

examples.output: Sink attached; metrics printed to console upon execution
examples.notes: print() outputs to stdout for debugging or monitoring

metadata.prompt: Call sink methods on a finalized DataStream to write results to an external system. Common sink operations include writeAsText(path) for file output and print() for console output. The sink is attached to the DataStream and executes when the job runs.

skill_drafts.name: Execute Flink Job and Retrieve Results
skill_drafts.description: Trigger job execution on the configured StreamExecutionEnvironment and optionally wait for completion to retrieve execution metrics and accumulator results.
applicable_signals: Caller requires execution results or job handle
Synchronous or asynchronous execution mode selected
contraindications: Still adding sources or sinks to the pipeline
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Verify pipeline is complete with sources, transformations, and sinks', 'condition': 'All DataStream operations defined'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Choose execution mode: synchronous via execute() or asynchronous via executeAsync()', 'condition': 'Caller determines blocking vs. non-blocking requirement'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Call execute() on StreamExecutionEnvironment to submit and wait for completion', 'condition': 'Synchronous execution desired; returns JobExecutionResult'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Alternatively, call executeAsync() to submit without blocking', 'condition': 'Asynchronous execution desired; returns JobClient'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Retrieve results via JobExecutionResult (synchronous) or jobClient.getJobExecutionResult().get() (asynchronous)', 'condition': 'Job execution complete or results needed'}
triggers: All sources, transformations, and sinks are defined in the DataStream pipeline
Ready to run the job and need execution metrics
Need to obtain a JobClient for asynchronous monitoring
constraints: StreamExecutionEnvironment must be configured before calling execute() or executeAsync()
All DataStream transformations and sinks must be defined
Execution will block (synchronous) or return immediately with a JobClient (asynchronous)
cautions: execute() blocks until job completion; use executeAsync() for non-blocking submission
JobExecutionResult is only available after job completion
Accumulator results are populated only if accumulators were registered in the job
output_contract: Returns JobExecutionResult containing execution times and accumulator results (synchronous mode), or JobClient handle for asynchronous monitoring and later result retrieval.

examples.input: StreamExecutionEnvironment with complete pipeline (sources, map transformation, text sink)
examples.output: JobExecutionResult with execution duration and any registered accumulator values
examples.notes: Synchronous execution; caller blocks until job finishes

examples.input: StreamExecutionEnvironment with complete pipeline; caller needs non-blocking submission
examples.output: JobClient; caller later calls getJobExecutionResult().get() to retrieve JobExecutionResult
examples.notes: Asynchronous execution; caller can perform other work while job runs

metadata.prompt: Call execute() on the StreamExecutionEnvironment to submit the job synchronously and block until completion, returning a JobExecutionResult. Alternatively, call executeAsync() to submit asynchronously and obtain a JobClient, then call getJobExecutionResult().get() on the client to retrieve results when ready. The JobExecutionResult contains execution times and accumulator values.
